blocks.markdown: # Email Sift Rubric

Sift labels new Gmail by importance on a schedule, and reads this doc in full before every run. It's my definition of what matters. Every rule above "Added by sift" is mine, and sift never changes those. Keep it under about two pages.
Timezone: America/Chicago
## How to use this doc

- **Change a rule:** edit any section above "Added by sift". Sift never changes those.
- **Correct a label:** in Gmail, swap the AI label for the right one, or add AI/Wrong. Sift learns from it on its next run and records the change in the Changelog.
- **Answer a question:** sift asks in comments that start with "Sift:". Reply in the thread, and the next run applies your answer.
- **Allow more than labels:** add it under Permissions, for example "Archive threads labeled AI/Junk".
- **Tell sift about yourself:** add notes under About me, grouped by topic. Sift adds its own notes there too, each starting with "(inferred)". Edit one to correct it, or remove "(inferred)" to make it yours.
## Labels

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| AI/Important | I'd want to see it today |
| AI/Low priority | Legitimate, nothing urgent |
| AI/Junk | Mail I never want |
| AI/Needs reply | Someone is waiting on me |
| AI/Sifted | Sift has evaluated it |
| AI/Wrong | I add this to flag a bad call |
## About me

Who I am, the people in my mail, and what matters to me right now, grouped by topic so related notes sit together. Sift reads this before every run. Lines I write are mine. Sift adds lines that start with "(inferred)", with where it learned each one and when, and it edits only those lines.
### (topic, such as Kids' soccer, Home, or Work)
- (I add these)
## Always important
Senders, topics, or situations that should always get AI/Important.

- Anything from a person I have written to in the last 90 days, unless it is clearly bulk mail
- Deadlines, payments, or schedule changes affecting the next 7 days
- Anything from my kids' coaches or teachers
- Anything about my mom's care, from anyone, is Important
## Needs reply
What counts as someone waiting on me specifically. It depends on the message, not on who sent it.

- A direct question addressed to me by name or as the only recipient
- Requests for a decision, approval, or volunteer sign-up
- A statement addressed to me that needs me to acknowledge it, such as a confirmation someone is waiting on
Not a reply, even from someone I know:

- A message to a group that only shares information, such as a note to all tenants about a visit
- An acknowledgment of my own message, such as "ok, thanks" or "got it"
## Low priority
Legitimate mail that doesn't meet the rules above, including:

- Automated notifications that only confirm something already done
- Group threads where I am Cc'd and nothing is asked of me
- Newsletters I signed up for
- Receipts and statements
- Social network notifications
## Junk
Mail I never want, including:

- Promotions and marketing I didn't ask for, even when worded urgently
- Spam-like or phishing-like messages

What sift did on each run, newest first, so I can check any call. To correct one, change its label in Gmail (see the rubric's "How to use this doc").
## Runs
Each run adds its date and time, a short summary, then one line per thread:
time | thread id | sender | subject | labels applied | reason
Times are in the timezone the rubric names.
